name: ALN-6222

card.summary: An experimental INHBE-targeting RNAi drug that has just entered its first obesity trial; nothing is known about results.
card.note: Investigational only; no published human data.

quick.overview:
ALN-6222 is an experimental RNA interference drug aimed at the INHBE gene and is in an early Phase 1 trial for obesity.

No results exist yet.
quick.mechanism: RNAi drugs lower production of a chosen protein by silencing its gene; the target here is INHBE.
quick.risks: No safety data have been reported. The drug is investigational and not available by prescription.

lead: ALN-6222 is an investigational RNA interference (RNAi) therapy that targets INHBE, a gene linked to fat distribution, in people with obesity [1]. The appearance interest is body composition: a drug that acts on fat distribution and fat mass could, if it works as intended, change where and how much fat a person carries, which shows in waist, midsection and overall leanness. It is not approved for any use.

Its public footprint is a Phase 1 trial registration (NCT07624071), which started on 4 June 2026, is recruiting, and plans to enroll 88 participants with obesity [1]. No results have been reported. RNAi drugs work by silencing the production of a chosen protein; the first RNAi therapeutic approved by the FDA was patisiran in 2018, and inclisiran (Leqvio) was approved in December 2021 to lower LDL cholesterol [2].

chain: Fat distribution and fat storage may change
angle.text: The idea behind targeting INHBE is to influence how the body stores fat. The drug is at first-in-human testing stage, and any appearance effect is hypothetical until trial results appear.

paras: ALN-6222 is described as an RNAi therapy directed at INHBE, a gene linked to fat distribution [1]. RNAi drugs of this type reduce the amount of a target protein made by cells, and approved examples such as patisiran and inclisiran show the platform in other conditions [2].
One Phase 1 trial in participants with obesity (88 planned) is registered and recruiting, having started on 4 June 2026 [1]. No results have been published.
